A1.justification: Both PDFs are 18-page versions of the same work. Their text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-training and generalization experiments, including empirical verification of theory, noise tests, and grid-resolution studies in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the generalization heatmaps, learned-operator visualizations, and repeated-seed and grid-resolution analyses.

M1.justification: The model formulations, training objectives, cross-function-space evaluation procedure, and Green’s-function extraction method are unchanged. The added corollary does not modify any method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same polynomial, sine, cosine, and piecewise-linear datasets, with the same 1D Poisson, biharmonic, 2D Poisson, noisy-data, and grid-resolution scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparison membership is unchanged: finite-difference fitting, PINN, linear, deep linear, MLP, DeepONet, Fourier Neural Operator, and Physics-Informed DeepONet retain their respective evaluations.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the 10,000-example datasets, normalization, N_grid = 22 cross-evaluation, MSE metric, and selection by best training MSE. Appendix B’s model configurations and training budgets also match.

E4.justification: Noise tests, Green’s-function visualizations, hardware/precision checks, and grid-size analyses are retained without changes. Appendix D’s relocation does not add or remove an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means and min–max spreads in Figure 3 and Appendix C, with the same seed information and reporting practices.

E6.justification: The experimental curves, heatmaps, numerical statements, and qualitative findings in Section 4 and Appendices C–D are unchanged. Figure 12 is repositioned without changing its results.

T1.justification: After Appendix A.3, v4 adds a loose relative Frobenius-error bound, Eq. (44), with factor sqrt(N_grid-(p+1)) and dependence on initialization magnitude. Its new proof uses the complementary projector and norm inequalities. The existing theorems, proofs, and Appendix A.4 estimate are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about function-space generalization limits, contrasting model behavior, Green’s-function interpretability, and cross-validation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of generalization failures, noise effects, and learned operators are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same linear-PDE scope and acknowledgment that the work characterizes failures without proposing a remedy.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same libraries, hardware, precision checks, architectures, optimizer settings, batch sizes, and learning-rate schedules. Code and data access information does not change.

R1.justification: The background discussion and reference list match after accounting for page reflow. No cited works or substantive research-positioning statements are added or removed.

P1.justification: The affiliation footnote now clarifies that OpenAI is the current affiliation and the work predates joining. A short corollary passage is inserted, while Appendix D’s unchanged text moves from page 15 to page 17; the broader narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: The longer affiliation note and added corollary cause local page reflow. Figure 12 moves upward on page 17 to accommodate Appendix D’s text below it. Figure content, axes, legends, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added appendix corollary turns the existing projection formula into an explicit, proved relative-error bound involving basis dimension and initialization, making that consequence easier to assess. This is a limited theoretical clarification: the bound is deliberately loose, and the main results and experimental evidence remain unchanged.
